_doc: skin.json for the customer-story template: a POINTER, not a skin. new-film writes `skin` into film.json "skin"; build_film.py
then runs tools/skin_apply.py (scenes/skin_data.js + design.md tokens) before the lint and the render.
Paper: warm paper ground, serif display, oxblood accent, calm motion profile, ink captions - a story watched in a bright room.
LIGHT GROUND: the skin's black token equals its paper, so the scene's #black plate (var(--black)) opens the film from the
paper, never from a dark flash; build_film.py checks the first rendered frame against it and export.py dips the booth loop to it.
Noir is the dark alternative (same calm profile, documentary captions).
head_fade: light skin: the plate is the paper (#F4F1EA); switch to noir and it is near-black again - nothing in the scene changes
